title: Late Charges on Retail Installment Contracts: Eligibility, Grace Period and Limits
content:
**Status.** On Retail Installment Contracts, a late charge may be assessed only while the contract status is active.

**Grace period.** A late charge on an installment may be assessed only when the assessment date is later than the installment due date plus the late-charge grace days. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the installment due date, and the installment due date is the contract's next due date for the oldest unpaid installment.

**Unpaid installment and no pyramiding.** An installment is unpaid when its due date is on or after the next due date. An installment satisfied by installment credit within its grace period never carries a late charge, even when an earlier late charge or other fee is still unpaid (the Federal Trade Commission Credit Practices Rule, 16 CFR 444.4, forbids pyramiding late charges).

**One per installment.** At most the tier's maximum number of late charges per installment — one — is assessed on one installment due date; the check is made on the contract's late charges recorded for that installment due date.

**Amount.** The clause "The late charge is the lesser of late charge percent of the scheduled payment and the late-charge cap, rounded half-up to the cent; it is recorded with the installment due date set to the installment's due date" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for working out the late charge on an installment.

**Deferred installments.** Installments deferred by an extension are not due until their new due dates and carry no late charge for the deferred months.

## Boundary of the grace period (hypothetical dates, grace of 10 days)

| Installment due date | Day 1 of grace | Last day of grace | Earliest assessment date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 June | 6 June | 15 June | 16 June |
| 28 February (non-leap year) | 1 March | 10 March | 11 March |

An assessment dated on the last day of grace (15 June in the first row) is not later than the due date plus 10 days and is not allowed; an assessment the next day is.

**Points of judgement.**

- A contract in repossessed or charged-off status carries no new late charge, whatever its days past due.
- If the borrower's payment on 12 June gives enough installment credit to satisfy the 5 June installment, that installment carries no late charge, even though an older late charge is still owed.

superseded_clauses: The late charge is the lesser of late_charge_pct of scheduled_payment_usd and late_charge_cap_usd, rounded half-up to the cent; it is recorded with installment_due_date set to the installment's due date.
